title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, and Upgrade / Rollback Procedures
author: Michael Chen
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices, reference architectures, and operational procedures for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, and customer operations teams who will install, operate, and upgrade Redwood Private in customer-managed networks or on-prem environments. The guide covers: prerequisites and customer requirements, three reference architectures (small, medium, large), on-prem packaging and compatibility, day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, capacity), and upgrade & rollback playbooks (canary, preflight checks, rollback steps).

Audience:
- Platform / SRE teams responsible for customer private deployments
- Solutions and Sales Engineers validating customer requirements
- Customer IT / Security teams performing installation and day-2 operations

Scope:
Covers VPC deployments (cloud customer VPC with private connectivity to Redwood control plane) and on-prem air-gapped installations supported by Redwood packaging. Excludes hoster-managed dedicated clusters and experimental deployment patterns.

1) High-level architecture:
Redwood Private is delivered as a control plane (hosted or customer-managed) plus a runtime plane that runs in customer infrastructure. Common components: control plane connector (outbound TLS), runtime nodes (GPU/CPU workers), edge/ingress proxies (mTLS/API gateway), and shared services (metrics exporters, tracing, local caching, optional model artifact store).

Design principles:
- Default to zero inbound firewall rules for cloud VPC installs; require outbound TLS to control plane endpoints.
- Least privilege for service accounts and KMS keys.
- Observable, auditable upgrades with preflight checks and automated rollback triggers.

2) Prerequisites and customer requirements (checklist):
Networking & connectivity:
- Network diagram, peering/VPN details, and security contact.
- Outbound HTTPS (443) to control plane endpoints; for restricted networks, use allowlist of IP ranges/FQDNs.
- Optional inbound endpoints for PrivateLink/Transit Gateway if private endpoints required.

Compute & storage:
- GPU nodes: recommended NVIDIA H100/A100 family; drivers must match packaging compatibility.
- CPU-only lab/test: 32 vCPU, 256 GB RAM minimum for minimal bundle.
- Persistent storage: NVMe for model caching; NFS or S3-compatible object store for artifacts.

Security & compliance:
- KMS/HSM for key material recommended.
- RBAC mapping and LDAP/Okta SSO integration.
- Audit logging retention and SIEM integration endpoints.

Operational:
- Identities for install (SSH bastion) and time-bound API keys for Redwood support.
- Capacity targets: expected RPS, request token distributions, concurrency targets.
- Maintenance windows for upgrades and network changes.

Short customer requirements checklist:
1. Network diagram and security contact.
2. IP allowlist and proxy configuration.
3. GPU SKU and driver versions.
4. Storage endpoints and retention policy.
5. SSO / identity provider details.
6. SLA and escalation owners.

3) Reference architectures:
3.1 Small (PoC / Labs):
- Topology: Single control plane + single runtime cluster (3 workers).
- Hardware: 3x A10G/A6000 or 1x H100 for model testing.
- SLOs: p95 < 2s for short prompts (<=512 tokens). Throughput: up to ~50 concurrent requests depending on model.
- Use: Proof of concept and integration testing.

3.2 Medium (Production / Team):
- Topology: Separate control plane subnets, dedicated runtime pools per model class, ingress proxies, internal metrics collectors.
- Hardware: 4-8x A100/H100 mixed pools; autoscaler for burst capacity using spot or spare nodes.
- SLOs: p95 < 500ms for short prompts; error rate p99 < 0.1%.
- Notes: Enable model caching and prefix caching layers.

3.3 Large (Enterprise / Multi-tenant):
- Topology: Multi-region control plane endpoints, per-tenant runtime pools, cross-region fallback, regional GPU fleets and artifact sync.
- Hardware: 16+ H100 or sharded clusters; dedicated inference fabric.
- SLOs: Multi-region failover within 30s; monitor 99.9th tail latencies.
- Notes: Separate tenant networks and storage; E2E encryption and customer KMS/HSM.

4) On-prem packaging and compatibility:
Packaging formats:
- OVA/VM image bundle (vSphere) for air-gapped installs.
- Helm charts + OCI images for Kubernetes (tested on EKS/GKE/AKS and on-prem K8s v1.26+).
- Bare-metal systemd packages for racked GPU servers without K8s.

Compatibility (abbreviated):
- Kubernetes: v1.24-1.29 (recommend 1.26+). CNI: Calico or Cilium.
- NVIDIA drivers: 535.xx - 555.xx depending on image version. Mellanox OFED 5.x for IB setups.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS; RHEL 8.9 supported.

Packaging notes:
- Air-gapped installs use signed artifact bundles and offline installer with checksums.
- Helm charts support values.yaml overrides for node selectors, tolerations, and device plugins.
- Packaging script generates node-level manifests for bare-metal installs.

5) Deployment procedure (cloud VPC and on-prem):
Pre-install (1-3 days planning):
1. Validate customer checklist.
2. Exchange public keys/certificates for TLS and mTLS.
3. Provide control plane endpoint URLs and IP allowlists.
4. Schedule maintenance window and support call.

Install steps (K8s Helm example):
1. kubectl create ns redwood-private
2. Configure values.yaml with control plane endpoint, image repo, storage backend, and node selectors.
3. helm upgrade --install redwood-private ./charts/redwood-private -n redwood-private -f values.yaml
4. kubectl get pods -n redwood-private (expect control-plane, runtime-manager, ingress-proxy, exporters)
5. Smoke tests: curl <internal-ingress>/healthz and run a short model exec test.

Bare-metal install (systemd example):
1. Run packaging script on each node to install runtime and device plugin.
2. sudo systemctl enable --now redwood-runtime redwood-exporter
3. Register node to runtime-manager with join token from preinstall.

Post-install validation checklist:
- Health endpoints OK for control plane and runtime.
- Metrics ingestion into Prometheus or forwarder.
- Model sandbox run via internal ingress with a 32-token prompt.

6) Day-2 operations:
Monitoring & alerting:
- Export metrics to Prometheus and forward to Grafana/Datadog. Key metrics: requests_per_minute, tokens_per_minute, request_latency_p50/p95/p99, model_load_time, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Recommended alerts: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m (P2), gpu_utilization > 95% for 10m (P2), error_rate > 0.5% for 5m (P1).

Backups & artifacts:
- Daily snapshot of model artifact store for production; object store lifecycle policies for retention.
- Export config snapshots (Helm values.yaml, runtime manager configs) before changes.

Scaling and capacity:
- Horizontal: add worker nodes and register to runtime manager; use cluster autoscaler and custom GPU autoscaler.
- Vertical: update resource requests/limits and restart pods during maintenance window.

Incident handling (brief):
1. Identify affected component via alerts/dashboards.
2. Triage with runbooks: restart exporter < runtime-manager < runtime-node.
3. For model regressions: rollback via control plane and notify ML owner.

7) Upgrade and rollback procedures:
Principles:
- Run preflight checks and config diff before upgrade.
- Use canary rollouts for control plane and runtime changes.
- Automate rollback on liveness or metric regressions.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Snapshot configs and stores (Helm values, DB snapshot, artifact manifest).
- Verify operator/test harness passing on staging that mirrors production.
- Notify stakeholders and schedule support window.

Canary upgrade (recommended):
1. Deploy new images to canary namespace or single runtime pool.
2. Run synthetic workload for 15-30 minutes and validate: p95 latency within 10% of baseline, error rate < 0.1%, model output quality smoke tests pass.
3. If canary passes, rollout progressively (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 10-15 minute observation windows.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
1. If canary or rollout triggers alert, revert traffic to previous stable pool via control plane.
2. For control plane rollbacks, restore last stable image and apply config snapshot.
3. Create postmortem and capture telemetry for RCA.

Rollback validation:
- Confirm traffic served from stable pool.
- Run smoke tests and model quality checks.
- Monitor metrics for 30 minutes before declaring resolved.

8) Customer requirements library (detailed checklist):
Network:
- Allowed outbound destinations (FQDN/IP) and proxy configuration.
- Load balancer/private endpoint architecture and certificates.

Compute & storage:
- GPU SKU and driver versions.
- Minimum NVMe disk performance (IOPS/throughput targets).
- Object store endpoints and credential management patterns.

Security:
- KMS provider, key rotation policy, HSM availability.
- Identity provider: SAML/OIDC, attribute mappings for RBAC.
- Audit log retention and SIEM integration.

Compliance:
- Data residency constraints for artifacts and logs.
- Data retention and purge policies for request logs and model artifacts.

Operational:
- Maintenance window cadence and escalation path.
- Contact matrix (support rotation, oncall names/emails, SLAs).
- Disaster recovery RTO/RPO objectives.

9) Troubleshooting & runbooks (links):
Common runbooks: node join failure (check device plugin and drivers), model load failures (artifact store credentials/checksum), high tail latency (analyze batch sizes, KV cache hits, GPU contention).
Related runbooks and incident playbooks: confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-deployment-day2-ops-upgrade-rollback-2026-10-12, confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-runbook-2028-03-01.

10) Appendix:
A) Control plane outbound endpoints: provide allowlist to Redwood SRE prior to install.
B) Example values.yaml snippet (helm):
apiVersion: v1
controlPlane:
  endpoint: "https://controlplane.example.redwood.internal"
  tls:
    caBundle: "<base64-encoded>"
runtime:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu: "true"
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "2000m"
      memory: "16Gi"

C) Contact & escalation:
- Redwood Private Operations: private-ops@redwood.example.com
- Oncall escalation: +1 555 0100 (pager) and support portal ticketing.
